devices.title: Prepare a USB stick for the Denon DJ Prime Go — Alpha-DJ-Engine
devices.h1: A gig-ready USB stick for your Denon Prime Go
devices.description: Alpha-DJ-Engine analyzes your tracks, builds a harmonic set and writes an Engine DJ USB the Prime Go plays natively — no Engine DJ desktop needed.
devices.intro: The Prime Go is our reference device — every Alpha release is tested on one before it ships. Point Alpha at a folder of tracks, pick the energy arc your night should follow, and the stick comes out analyzed, harmonically ordered and ready to play the moment it clicks into the Prime Go's USB port.
devices.deviceDetail: The Prime Go is a battery-powered two-deck standalone, and that is exactly the setup Alpha is built around: no laptop in the booth, just the unit and a prepared drive. It takes both USB sticks and SD cards, and the on-disk format Alpha writes is identical for either — point the export at whichever is mounted.
quirks: This is the device every Alpha release is validated on — if something works anywhere, it works here first.
The Prime Go re-analyzes nothing: Alpha's BPM, key and beatgrid are read as-is from the Engine library, so tracks are ready the moment they load.
If a playlist shows up without waveforms at first, that's normal — the Prime Go draws its own waveform the first time it loads a track.
Playing outdoors on battery? Prepare several playlists on one stick — Alpha adds to the Engine library on the drive, it never wipes it.

faq.q: Do I need the Engine DJ desktop app to prepare a stick for the Prime Go?
faq.a: No. Alpha writes the Engine OS 3.x library directly onto the drive — the Prime Go mounts it exactly like a stick prepared by Engine DJ itself, with playlists, BPM and key in place.

faq.q: I'm coming from rekordbox — can the Prime Go use my rekordbox USB?
faq.a: Engine OS can import a rekordbox stick on the device, but that import is slow and beatgrids can shift. The cleaner way: export your collection as a rekordbox XML, let Alpha keep the BPM, key and beatgrid rekordbox worked out, and write a native Engine library to the stick instead.

faq.q: Can I use the Prime Go's SD card slot instead of a USB stick?
faq.a: Yes. Point Alpha's export at the mounted SD card — the on-disk format is identical, so the Prime Go reads either the same way.

faq.q: How should the stick be formatted for the Prime Go?
faq.a: exFAT (Denon's recommendation) or FAT32 — Engine OS does not read NTFS. Alpha writes onto the stick's existing filesystem; it never reformats your drive.

devices.title: Use the XDJ-1000MK2 without rekordbox — Alpha-DJ-Engine
devices.h1: A rekordbox USB for the XDJ-1000MK2 — no rekordbox needed
devices.description: Alpha-DJ-Engine writes the rekordbox library the XDJ-1000MK2 reads straight from USB — analyzed tracks, beat grids, waveforms, playlists. No rekordbox.
devices.intro: "Can I use the XDJ-1000MK2 without rekordbox?" is one of the most-asked questions about this player — and the honest answer used to be "not really": raw MP3s on a stick load with half-empty waveforms and no grids. Alpha changes that answer. It writes the full rekordbox library the player expects, without rekordbox being installed anywhere.
devices.deviceDetail: The 1000MK2 is USB-only — no SD slot, no disc drive — so the stick is the whole show. Alpha writes the complete rekordbox library onto it: both database formats, per-track beat grids and waveforms, artwork, and your playlist in exactly the order you built.
quirks: Playing raw files without a library means no proper waveforms or grids on this player — that's why a written rekordbox library (Alpha's job) beats a plain folder of MP3s.
USB is the only media slot on the 1000MK2 — everything rides on a well-prepared stick.
FAT32 or HFS+ only — the 1000MK2's generation doesn't read exFAT or NTFS.

faq.q: Can I really use the XDJ-1000MK2 without rekordbox?
faq.a: Yes — with a prepared stick. Alpha writes the rekordbox database and ANLZ analysis files itself, so the player gets real beat grids, waveforms and playlists without rekordbox ever being installed.

faq.q: What happens if I just copy MP3s onto a stick?
faq.a: The player will play them, but with half-drawn waveforms, no beat grids and no playlists — browsing by folder only. A written library fixes all of that, and that's exactly what Alpha produces.

faq.q: What format should the stick be?
faq.a: FAT32 (or HFS+ on Mac) — this generation doesn't read exFAT. Alpha writes onto the existing filesystem and never reformats.

devices.title: XDJ-700 USB export — prepared without rekordbox — Alpha-DJ-Engine
devices.h1: A rekordbox USB for your XDJ-700
devices.description: Alpha-DJ-Engine writes the rekordbox USB export the XDJ-700 reads natively — tracks analyzed, harmonically ordered and loudness-matched. No rekordbox.
devices.intro: The XDJ-700 packs the CDJ workflow into the smallest touchscreen player Pioneer makes — perfect for home booths and tight setups. Alpha feeds it the way it wants to be fed: a rekordbox USB written directly from your computer, analyzed and sequenced before you ever touch the jog wheel.
devices.deviceDetail: Like its bigger siblings the XDJ-700 reads the rekordbox library straight from USB. Alpha writes the full package — both database formats, beat grids, waveforms, artwork, playlist order — so the compact screen browses a finished set, not a pile of files.
quirks: USB-only media: the XDJ-700 has no SD slot, so the prepared stick carries everything.
FAT32 (or HFS+ on Mac) is the format to use — exFAT support isn't part of this player's generation.
One constant beat grid per track; tempo changes inside a track aren't modelled.

faq.q: Does the XDJ-700 read Alpha's stick without rekordbox installed anywhere?
faq.a: Yes. Alpha writes the rekordbox database and analysis files itself; the XDJ-700 reads the stick natively.

faq.q: Is the XDJ-700 too small for a full prepared set?
faq.a: No — it reads the same rekordbox library as the CDJ-3000. Your whole set, playlists and analysis included, fits on one stick.

faq.q: Which format should the stick use?
faq.a: FAT32 — the safe choice for the 700's generation (HFS+ also works from a Mac). Alpha writes onto the existing filesystem and never reformats your drive.

devices.title: OPUS-QUAD USB export — no rekordbox required — Alpha-DJ-Engine
devices.h1: A rekordbox USB for your OPUS-QUAD — no rekordbox required
devices.description: Alpha-DJ-Engine writes both rekordbox libraries — including the newer Device Library Plus — straight to USB. The OPUS-QUAD reads it natively.
devices.intro: The OPUS-QUAD is AlphaTheta's statement piece — four decks, a 10.1-inch screen, and standalone playback that leans on the newer encrypted rekordbox library. Alpha writes exactly that library, straight from your computer, with your set analyzed and harmonically ordered before it ever reaches the booth.
devices.deviceDetail: As one of the newest players, the OPUS-QUAD prefers the encrypted exportLibrary.db — the format behind rekordbox's "Device Library Plus" — which Alpha writes alongside the classic export.pdb, so the same stick also plays on older CDJs and XDJs. Beat grids, waveforms, artwork and playlist order all land where the player looks for them.
quirks: The OPUS-QUAD leans on the newer encrypted library (Device Library Plus) — Alpha writes it natively, plus the classic one for older gear on the same stick.
Three USB slots: two up top for sticks, plus a faster rear port meant for an SSD — Alpha's library plays from any of them. There's no SD slot.
exFAT and FAT32 both work on the OPUS-QUAD; NTFS doesn't.

faq.q: Does the OPUS-QUAD read Alpha's stick without any rekordbox software?
faq.a: Yes. Alpha writes the rekordbox libraries and analysis files directly — the OPUS-QUAD reads the drive natively, subscription-free.

faq.q: What about Device Library Plus and the "rekordbox Database not found" error?
faq.a: The OPUS-QUAD generation reads the newer encrypted Device Library Plus database. Alpha writes it alongside the classic export.pdb, so the player finds its library instead of throwing that error at you.

faq.q: Can I plug an SSD into the rear USB port?
faq.a: Yes — the rear port is built for exactly that, and Alpha's library plays from an SSD the same as from a stick. Format it exFAT or FAT32.

devices.title: XDJ-AZ USB export — written on your computer — Alpha-DJ-Engine
devices.h1: A rekordbox USB for the XDJ-AZ, written on your computer
devices.description: Alpha-DJ-Engine builds a harmonic set and writes the rekordbox USB export the XDJ-AZ reads natively — including the newer Device Library Plus format.
devices.intro: The XDJ-AZ is AlphaTheta's newest full-size all-in-one — the four-channel booth that travels. Alpha prepares what it plays: a rekordbox USB written directly on your computer, with analysis, harmonic order and loudness handled before the gig, not during it.
devices.deviceDetail: As a current-generation player the XDJ-AZ reads the newer encrypted rekordbox library — Device Library Plus — which Alpha writes alongside the classic format: one stick for the AZ and for every older player you might encounter. Playlists arrive in set order with beat grids and waveforms ready.
quirks: Current-generation player, current-generation library: Alpha writes the encrypted Device Library Plus database the AZ prefers, plus the classic export.pdb for everything older.
The AZ re-analyzes nothing — grids and waveforms come from Alpha's ANLZ files and load instantly.
FAT32, exFAT and HFS+ all mount on the AZ; NTFS doesn't. There's no SD slot — it's USB only.

faq.q: Does the XDJ-AZ read Alpha's stick without rekordbox?
faq.a: Yes. Alpha writes the rekordbox database and analysis files itself; the AZ reads the stick natively — no software, no subscription.

faq.q: Is the XDJ-AZ too new for Alpha's export?
faq.a: No — Alpha writes the newer encrypted Device Library Plus library the latest players prefer, alongside the classic one. It is a new target though, so confirm on your own unit before a gig.

faq.q: Will my stick also work on club CDJs?
faq.a: Yes — both library formats are on the stick, so CDJ-3000s and older players read it too.

devices.compatNote: Alpha writes a VirtualDJ library onto the drive, which the VirtualDJ app on a Mac or PC then loads — so any controller VirtualDJ supports will play the set. It is not a standalone stick for the gear itself.
devices.metaOverride: Compatible · via VirtualDJ on a laptop

devices.compatNote: Alpha writes a Serato crate plus the beat grid onto the drive; plug it into a laptop running Serato DJ and the crate appears. Serato only scans a drive's root, so export to the root rather than a subfolder. Hot cues and loops are not written yet.
devices.metaOverride: Compatible · via Serato on a laptop

devices.compatNote: Alpha writes a collection.nml alongside the audio. Traktor does not scan drives by itself — import it once via File → Import Collection.
devices.metaOverride: Compatible · via Traktor on a laptop
